_comment: The analysis menu: investigation tasks grouped into sections, each answering one question.
A task lists the actions (from tools.json) that answer it. 'default' marks the actions ticked when the
task is chosen; the others can be added in the task's details. 'artifacts' narrows an action to some of
its artifact types within this task, so choosing 'Accounts and logons' runs RECmd on SAM hives only.
When several chosen tasks share an action, it runs once over the union of their inputs.
'icon' names a glyph defined in gui/theme.py; 'reading' tells the analyst where to start in the results.

sections.title: What happened
sections.about: Reconstruct what users and programs did on the system.

sections.title: Was it an attack
sections.about: Look for attacker techniques, suspicious programs and tampering.

sections.title: Dig deeper
sections.about: Full parses and utilities for detailed review.

tasks.title: Program execution
tasks.question: Which programs ran, when, and how often?
tasks.about: Combines four independent execution records: prefetch run counts and times, Amcache inventory with SHA-1 hashes, the ShimCache list in the SYSTEM hive, and the Windows 7 RecentFileCache.
tasks.reading: Start with the PECmd timeline: one row per run, sorted by time. Look up unfamiliar programs in the Amcache results by their SHA-1.

tasks.title: Files and folders opened
tasks.question: Which documents and folders did users open, and from which drives?
tasks.about: Shortcut files and jump lists record documents users opened; ShellBags record the folders they browsed, even on removed USB drives; the Windows Search index lists files it has seen.
tasks.reading: LECmd and JLECmd results show the target path, its timestamps and the volume serial number. ShellBags show folder paths with first and last interaction times.

tasks.title: Accounts and logons
tasks.question: Who logged on, how, and from where?
tasks.about: Summarises successful and failed logons from the Security event log, lists local accounts from the SAM hive, and reads User Access Logging on Windows Server.
tasks.reading: The Hayabusa logon summary counts logons per user, logon type and source address. Logon type 10 is RDP; type 3 is network.

tasks.title: File system timeline
tasks.question: What was created, changed, renamed or deleted on the volume?
tasks.about: Parses the NTFS Master File Table into one row per file with all timestamps, and the USN change journal into every create, rename, write and delete it recorded.
tasks.reading: Open the $MFT output in Timeline Explorer and filter by path or extension. The $J output lists changes in order; its paths are complete when the $MFT of the same volume was present.

tasks.title: Deleted files
tasks.question: What was deleted, from where, and when?
tasks.about: Recycle Bin records keep each deleted file's original path, size and deletion time. The USN journal also records deletions that bypassed the Recycle Bin.
tasks.reading: RBCmd lists one row per deleted file. Search the USN journal output for the reason FileDelete to find the rest.

tasks.title: Application and network usage
tasks.question: How long were applications used, and how much did each send over the network?
tasks.about: SRUM keeps about 30 days of per-application CPU time and network traffic. The Windows Timeline records which applications and documents had focus, and for how long.
tasks.reading: In the SRUM network usage table, sort by bytes sent to spot large uploads. The Timeline output shows activity per application with start and end times.

tasks.title: Browser and app databases
tasks.question: Which sites were visited, what was downloaded, and what did apps store?
tasks.about: Runs known queries against SQLite databases of browsers, cloud sync clients, messaging and other applications.
tasks.reading: Each recognised database produces its own CSV named after the application and the data it holds, such as history, downloads or cookies.

tasks.title: Threat detection
tasks.question: Do the event logs show known attacker techniques?
tasks.about: Hayabusa applies thousands of Sigma rules to the event logs and writes a timeline of detections with severity levels and MITRE ATT&CK tags. Chainsaw can hunt with a second rule set.
tasks.reading: Open the Hayabusa HTML summary first for the overall picture, then the timeline CSV. Review critical and high detections before the rest.

tasks.title: Event log review
tasks.question: What did the logs record, and were they cleared or tampered with?
tasks.about: Normalises every event into one CSV with the useful fields extracted, counts events per ID, and looks for gaps in record numbers and time that suggest deleted records.
tasks.reading: The EvtxECmd CSV is best explored in Timeline Explorer, grouped by Channel and Event Id. Any gap Chainsaw reports deserves a closer look.

tasks.title: Executable triage
tasks.question: Are these programs signed, packed, or hiding something?
tasks.about: Checks digital signatures and hashes, identifies the compiler and any packer or protector, and can recover obfuscated strings with FLOSS.
tasks.reading: Unsigned files and files identified as packed are the first to examine. Hashes from Sigcheck can be looked up in threat intelligence services.

tasks.title: Memory analysis
tasks.question: What was running at capture time: processes, connections, injected code?
tasks.about: Volatility 3 lists processes (including hidden ones), their command lines, network connections and services, and flags memory regions that look like injected code.
tasks.reading: Compare the process list with the process scan: processes only in the scan were hidden or have exited. Malfind hits show executable memory that is not backed by a file.

tasks.title: Registry deep dive
tasks.question: What do the hives record about the system, its users and devices?
tasks.about: Extracts the forensically relevant keys of every hive with RECmd. RegRipper writes a readable report per hive, and rla produces clean hive copies with transaction logs applied.
tasks.reading: The RECmd batch CSV has one row per finding with a category column; filter by category such as Devices, User Activity or Persistence.

tasks.title: Document and media metadata
tasks.question: Who authored a document, and when and where was a photo taken?
tasks.about: Reads the metadata of documents, photos, audio and video: authors, software, creation times, camera models and GPS positions.
tasks.reading: Each row is one file. Useful columns include Author, Creator, CreateDate, Make, Model and the GPS fields.

tasks.title: Strings
tasks.question: Which readable text, addresses or paths does a file contain?
tasks.about: Extracts ASCII and Unicode strings from any file. Best used on a few selected files, as it runs once per file.
tasks.reading: Each file gets its own text file of strings. Search them for URLs, IP addresses, paths or user names.
